title: How does a barcode tell a scanner what you bought?
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

lines.text: When you scan an item at the supermarket checkout, what is the red laser actually reading?
lines.caps: What is the *red laser | actually reading on a *barcode?

lines.text: Most people think the scanner reads the black bars, but it is actually reading the white spaces.
lines.caps: The scanner reads the *white spaces | not the black *bars!

lines.text: A red laser sweeps across the code, and a light sensor measures reflected light intensity.
lines.caps: A red laser sweeps *across | measuring reflected *light

lines.text: Black bars absorb laser light while white spaces reflect it back as a pattern of ones and zeros.
This binary sequence translates into a twelve-digit Universal Product Code number.
The register instantly looks up that code in the store database to pull up the product name and price.
lines.caps: Matches the code to the *price | in the *database!

lines.text: That simple pattern of stripes automated the entire global retail economy.
lines.caps: Stripes of ink that *power | the entire global *economy!
